published_prior_art.cite: Huwang1995 establishes the non-uniformity of a normal binomial interval; exact randomized inversion itself is standard, while the causal profiling application is not covered.
TianWu2025 gives efficient PN/PS inference under regular fixed-law conditions, not a triangular rare-conditioning-probability frontier.
GleserHwang1987 gives a general finite-expected-diameter impossibility template, not this bounded monotone PN submodel and effective-count rate.
MikushevaSun2022 develops weak-IV robust inversion in a distinct linear-IV experiment; TianWu2025 is regular-law PN/PS inference.
HannartNaveau2018 selects a climate index by causal evidence, but does not provide selected-event-honest learned-score confidence-set inversion.

novelty_flags.label: Related work / CaiKuroki2006
novelty_flags.one_line: The core calls this Cai and Kuroki (2006), but the cited Risk Analysis article is Cai and Kuroki (2005), vol. 25, pp. 1611–1620; correct the year even though the variance-estimation description is substantively accurate.

soundness_flags.label: def:finite-lr and thm:finite-experiment
soundness_flags.one_line: The calibration law draws support labels L_j randomly with probabilities w, whereas S_obs fixes L_j=j; thus the stated observed iid experiment is not a realization of P_xi, so exact coverage cannot follow without defining a genuine resampling experiment or conditioning and using the corresponding fixed-design likelihood.

soundness_flags.label: thm:lower
soundness_flags.one_line: d_n varies with P_n over M_n, but it is outside the supremum in the displayed normalized risk; fix a rarity schedule and use M_n(d_n), or place d(P_n) inside the supremum normalization.

soundness_flags.label: oeq:all-regime-transfer
soundness_flags.one_line: Its uniform diameter ratio repeats the law-dependent d_n-outside-supremum ambiguity, so the claimed target is not a defined uniform functional over M_n.

accepted_scope_caveats.label: thm:finite-experiment marked-Poisson conclusion
accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: The marked-Poisson limit is asserted only along finite-experiment sequences satisfying the explicitly declared joint marked-intensity and common-cell-profile convergence.
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: Marked-Poisson convergence conditional on those two convergence premises.

accepted_scope_caveats.label: thm:gaussian-recovery
accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: Continuous-law Gaussian recovery and shrinking diameter are restricted to M_n^{LAN}, including score nondegeneracy and the displayed smoothness-rarity domination condition.
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: O((n d_n)^(-1/2)) diameter only over M_n^{LAN}.

accepted_scope_caveats.label: PS conclusions
accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: PS is defined only when its protected factual conditioning probability is positive.
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: All PS analogues conditional on d_n^{PS}>0.

accepted_scope_caveats.label: def:finite-lr zero-denominator closure
accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: d(xi)=0 points are calibration limits and do not carry a PN parameter.
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: Finite-experiment PN coverage only for positive-denominator null laws.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Replace the random-label empirical-support experiment with either a conditional-on-X product-cell likelihood or an explicitly randomized sampling scheme whose observed statistic is distributed as P_xi; then restate finite coverage for that same experiment.
Index every uniform theorem by a fixed rarity schedule d_n, defining M_n(d_n), and state the lower and all-regime ratios with that schedule rather than a law-dependent denominator outside a supremum.

Promote ZhangWangMiao2025 and LiMaoPearl2022 into the theorem-specific comparison for rare/uncertain PN inference, and state precisely why their partial-ID or sample-size settings do not subsume the proposed monotone point-ID frontier.

After repairing the sampling experiment, sharpen the headline to a same-class matched upper/lower theorem over M_n(d_n), with the all-regime transfer as the explicit remaining upper-bound route rather than treating the finite-profile result as observed-law coverage.

recommended_next_step: Revise the sampling experiment and fixed-rarity class first; then rerun novelty review with theorem-specific comparisons to modern PN inference.
